- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.3) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Forecast tends to lag the true price decline — especially after sharp drops, model holds too much momentum.
- After a spike in price, model overcorrects downward, then undercorrects — creates “overshoot + lag” pattern.
- Mean reversion bias: model often assumes price will return to historical mean too quickly, ignoring volatility clustering.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early stages of a downtrend — model doesn’t adjust for “sudden reversal” sentiment.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model overweights momentum — fails to account for regulatory or policy-induced corrections.
- Model underweights sentiment when it’s negative and price is falling — fails to recognize “panic” or “flight to safety” effects.
